notes: PHASE-000 foundation is complete and PHASE-001 development is active. WU-002 remains in progress because its acceptance criterion is not yet satisfied: approved desktop calling applications have not consumed processed/bypass audio through an installed OS-visible VSN virtual microphone. The verified Windows foundation includes Rust audio contracts and bounded queues, deterministic device selection/reselection, bounded stream recovery, IAudioClient3 planning, event-driven WASAPI capture, sample decode/reframing, CaptureRuntime reopen recovery, IMMNotificationClient delivery, bounded virtual-mic staging/output, Rust/C++ transport ABI, aligned Interlocked cursor publication, deterministic shared-region geometry, real user-mode section mapping and a WDK-buildable KMDF control driver with a secure driver-owned section lifecycle. The original caller-supplied-section CONNECT assumption was replaced by driver-owned CONNECT v2 in merge 3953069f468c46d744f30625b3696e5b12f03a77 after AI Native run 34537871677 and Windows run 34537871806 passed. The KMDF control-driver slice merged as b2761ad400d92c1d810751fabcf4b071a40dfb9c after AI Native run 34539554036 and Windows run 34539554115 passed. A concurrency review then identified that global producer/consumer cursors alone could not prove that a PCM slot was not being overwritten while the kernel copied it during an overrun. The transport protocol was therefore advanced to version 2 with one aligned 64-bit seqlock-style stamp per PCM slot. The shared region places the slot-stamp array at offset 128 and audio at offset 192; the 48 kHz mono F32 10 ms four-frame reference mapping is 7,872 bytes. Producer helpers mark a slot writing before PCM mutation and publish a stable sequence stamp only after the complete frame write. ConsumeOneRingFrame uses the immutable CONNECT-time ProtocolHeader retained by the driver, normalizes overrun cursors with exact drop accounting, emits fresh silence on underrun without advancing the consumer, validates the target slot stamp before and after copying PCM, rejects a concurrently reused/torn slot without advancing the consumer and has no unbounded retry loop. AI Native Quality Gates run 34541120876 and Windows Audio Validation run 34541120903 passed the protocol-v2 guarded-consumer slice, which merged as 9c57207482bdc20ca5dc70a06cbb43c0cfa86741. The next implementation added a compile-verified PortCls/WaveRT descriptor scaffold aligned to the existing shared-ring format: 48 kHz, mono, 32-bit IEEE float, one capture stream, a wave bridge plus host capture pin and ADC node, and a minimal microphone-source-to-wave-bridge topology. The WDK project now links the PortCls/stdunk/libcntpr libraries and compiles those KS/PortCls descriptors into the same .sys build while a native contract test locks the initial sample rate, channel count, sample width, byte rate and descriptor indices. AI Native Quality Gates run 34542011551 and Windows Audio Validation run 34542011553 both passed on implementation head c3fc7b77593ebd99c98dfbf71cf32532c2645742; Windows passed Rust compile/Clippy/tests, WDK restore, the KMDF .sys build/validation and the expanded C++ suite including the WaveRT descriptor contract. This descriptor slice merged as da1b0543bcbfe63ff6a342690cab3b250057bbe2. This proves build-valid PortCls/WaveRT endpoint descriptors only. It does not yet prove PortCls miniport registration, a WaveRT stream object, audio-engine position/notification behavior, INF/package installation, an OS-visible microphone or calling-app compatibility. Still pending are miniport/adapter registration, stream lifecycle and guarded-ring binding, INF/package installation and test signing on a controlled Windows machine, endpoint enumeration and runtime DeviceIoControl evidence, least-privilege non-admin broker/interface policy, processed/bypass audio reaching approved calling applications, physical-device recovery evidence, hardware CPU/latency/jitter/deadline measurements, and production signing/update/uninstall/rollback verification. The next valid WU-002 action is to implement the minimal PortCls adapter/miniport registration and WaveRT capture-stream lifecycle around the verified descriptors, binding the stream-copy boundary to ConsumeOneRingFrame while preserving fresh-silence underrun and generation fencing; no OS-visible endpoint claim is valid until install/enumeration/runtime evidence exists. Paid provider usage, proprietary model training, production credentials/cloud spend and production deployment remain subject to applicable provider/data/compute/release gates.
